title: Twenty questions × three steering scopes
description: Ten originally correct answers and ten selected made-up answers, with input-only, output-only and input + output steering. Tuned conversions of made-up answers: 10/10, 7/10 and 10/10 respectively. Includes all 1,176 positive trials, shared strengths, false abstentions and nonmonotonic examples.

title: Original abstention story and posters
description: Natural activation evidence plus the first ten selected made-up-answer cases: output steering produces coherent, grounded ‘I don’t know’ answers in 7/10 with question-specific strengths. Includes the failed bat-rabies example and the actual search procedure.

title: Three confidence-wording gates: 4 correct / 4 made up / 4 abstentions
description: L11–T652, L13–T2128 and L6–T1751 are zero throughout all twelve QA prompts and responses. All three activate on a separate confidence-wording control. These candidates did not provide an answer-confidence measure on these examples.

title: Seven uncertainty gates: the same 4 / 4 / 4 cases
description: Token heatmaps for questions and unsteered answers. Four candidates activate in all four natural abstentions and none of the eight correct/made-up responses. The priority three are zero on question tokens and the final input position; their response contrast is not a validated advance confidence signal.

title: Confidence and uncertainty label shortlist
description: Label-only search across 36 layers and 89,280 transform slots, including placeholders: 769 keyword matches, twelve refreshed candidate descriptions and the shortlist used above. Labels suggest candidates; no confidence–steering-strength correlation has been established.

title: Two-passage native baseline
description: Twenty questions, no steering: the model answers all ten answer-present questions correctly. Of ten answer-absent questions, it makes up an answer for four and withholds an answer for six. Some withholding explanations need separate factual review.

title: L19–T368 answer-token heatmaps
description: Native replay of the ten answer-absent responses: zero gate activity throughout all four made-up answers; some activity in each of the six withholding responses. Correlative evidence on emitted response tokens, with complete token and contribution measurements.

title: Absolute gate replacement, 0.5–3.5
description: Force L19–T368 to fixed gate values at processed output-token positions on the original four made-up answers. The electric-eel question becomes a coherent abstention at 3 and 3.5; the other three do not. This is absolute gate replacement.

title: Additive coefficients 3–8
description: Keep the native MLP and add the current-input low-rank output at each processed response token. The electric-eel case abstains at all tested additions; no further question converts through +8. This differs from fixing the gate to an absolute value.

title: Remaining three cases, additions 8–32
description: Minerals converts at +16–32 and crystallization at +24/32. Vampire-bat responses remain false or mixed. Preserves fluent failures separately from clear abstention successes.

title: All ten original answer-absent questions
description: Additive sweep at 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64, retaining both baseline groups: four made-up answers and six withholdings. Scatter panels track coherence, made-up answers and abstention decisions; all outputs collapse at 64.

title: Fresh Harvard / pharmacy screen
description: A fresh ten-question screen yields only one made-up baseline answer and nine withholdings. Kept as a negative screening result; the one conversion case does not become a clean abstention at 4–32, and coherence collapses at 64.

title: Four-case replay and fine vampire-bat search
description: The three earlier conversions reproduce at +24, +16 and +4. The remaining vampire-bat case has no clean abstention among 128 distinct strengths, 0.5–64 in steps of 0.5. Includes every response and the fluent-but-false near-misses.

title: Six additional made-up-answer cases
description: Screen 80 questions, freeze six clear baseline failures, then steer: 4/6 new clear conversions, bringing the original output-only total to 7/10. Complete screening judgments and failed or ambiguous cases are retained.

title: Correct answers: output-only steering
description: Ten questions whose answers are in the passage and are answered correctly at baseline. Output-only steering induces coherent withholding in 3/10 at some tested strength; many other responses reveal the answer before adding ‘I don’t know.’ Withholding here is false abstention.

title: Correct answers: input + output steering
description: Steer the full encoded input and processed response tokens on the same ten questions. Coherent answer-withholding is found in 7/10 with per-question tuning. Includes answer leakage, false explanations and timing comparisons.

title: Correct answers: input-only steering
description: Steer only the encoded input; decoding receives its modified cache but no output-token edits. Coherent withholding is found in 3/10 with tuning. Compares all three scopes; the completed shared-grid analysis is in the twenty-question report above.

title: Medical qualification pilot
description: Early L19–T368 study: 24 prompts screened, then component removal and negative steering. Ordinary symptom prompts were already answered and had no target activation. No clear refusal-to-answer switch was established.

title: Medical qualification: negative factor 16
description: Follow-up on six prompts with matched native controls. Factor −16 does not coherently remove qualification denial on the five active prompts; several openings become malformed. The inactive control remains unchanged.

title: Medical qualification: extended negative sweep
description: A closer sweep between −16 and −32 finds a fluent qualification affirmation at −30 for general guidance while retaining diagnosis/treatment limits. Other prompts break down. Changing qualification wording did not establish removal of the underlying medical limits.

title: L19–T368 in native safety refusals
description: Three fixed safety requests naturally produce refusals with gate activity. Includes shared-scale abstention references, complete native answers and token heatmaps. Observation only: no causal manipulation or general refusal-detection claim.
